Subject: Re: Greenline prod — urgent: 504/429 spike after 07:45 deploy (logs attached)

Investigation summary (quick):
- Root signal: elevated cache eviction rate starting at 07:41 UTC (local 07:41 PST) coincident with the batching heuristic rollout in v1.14.2. Evictions for prefix keys rose ~30x.
- Mechanism: a batching "coalescer" change left ~10% of batches "orphaned" (requests that entered batch coordination but were never dispatched due to a race). Those requests sat in the local dispatcher queue, holding KV-cache slots (sticky entries) and preventing effective cache locality. This caused queue amplification — more inflight requests waiting, which in turn increased memory pressure and eviction churn.
- Amplification: client-side retry loops made the effective arrival rate spike; we observed retry storms that turned a ~2x load into a ~6-8x transient. 429s spiked when our per-worker rate limiter tripped, and 504s downstream when the serving queue topped out.
- Metrics: p50 ~350ms -> 1.1s, p95 ~1.4s -> 3.8s, p99 ~1.9s -> 9.2s. 504 rate from 0.3% -> ~12% during the 07:50-08:05 window.

Immediate mitigation applied (09:00 PST):
1) Disabled the new batching coalescer for the Greenline route (feature toggle).
2) Forced a delayed eviction pass that freed sticky keys tied to orphaned batches.
3) Applied a temporary stricter per-client retry-window (backoff) via config to reduce amplification.
4) Enabled fallback to baseline (untuned) model variant for high-latency requests.

Current status: 504 rate down to ~0.9%, p99 returned to ~1.5s within 10-12 minutes of mitigations. No data loss detected.

Follow-ups (next 24h):
- Root-cause PR to revert the coalescer race and add stronger invariants (owner: eng/batching team).
- Add a canary guard: when eviction rate or orphaned-batch count exceeds X, auto-disable batching for affected routes.
- Postmortem and diff-level tests for eviction/queue interactions (owner: Marissa).

I've attached a KV snapshot we captured (kv_cache_snapshot_1129.txt) and a short timeline in the incident channel. Happy to jump on a call with Greenline if you want me to walk through technical details.

— Markus
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
